segments.text: In a right triangle, the square built on the hypotenuse matches the combined area of the squares built on the two legs.
Construct three squares, one on each side of the triangle, so that the geometric comparison is expressed by explicit figures.
The target equality is that the area attached to the hypotenuse equals the two leg-squares taken together.
Euclid’s proof route proceeds through area-preserving comparisons of auxiliary figures and then combines equalities.
The final relation is the familiar Pythagorean statement, expressed here as a synchronized English explanation layer.
